body:
## Question

How can realistic multi-source catalogues reconcile, be inspected and publish safely beyond the reproduced 16 MiB image-bearing candidate ceiling and ten-second CLI request deadline? Evaluate immutable object references, partitioned candidate manifests, bounded reconciliation/diff/export/image work, durable approval operations and status/retry, final atomic visibility, stale approval fencing, applicability-date changes, concurrency/supersession, idempotency, recovery and orphan cleanup. Avoid a metadata-only replacement that still buffers the entire catalogue. Specify measurable byte/work/memory/request budgets, realistic full-game and second-publisher workload targets and failure tests; no invented measured throughput. Resolve cost/platform constraints through current primary documentation when needed. Architectural topology remains a proposal until this decision.

comments.body:
## Owner-approved scope amendment — card content without tournament eligibility

The owner explicitly does not intend to consume tournament eligibility, ban lists, organised-play restrictions, FAQs or rulings. After distinguishing those from card content, the owner agreed to retain publisher corrections alongside original printed text. This scope decision is settled; the wider durable publication decision remains open.

Across all Supported Games, exclude acquisition and normalization of tournament policy as a required catalogue capability, Legality Rules, derived Legality Status, tournament applicability and unresolved-target-scope processing, eligibility APIs/CLI operations/export components, and their publication gates. Omit these contracts rather than returning permanent “unknown” eligibility. An unavailable or unparseable ban-list or tournament-policy source must not block card ingestion or publication in the replacement design.

Retain Printed Rules Text, including restrictions actually printed on the card; publisher-issued Errata and Effective Rules Text alongside the original; physical printed markings; and Product/Release/Distribution Context facts. These describe cards and releases without interpreting organised-play eligibility. General FAQs/rulings are not a catalogue feature or required acquisition surface. Explicit unknowns remain for in-scope card facts. Supporting evidence, identity/history, source coverage and recovery protections remain required.

This supersedes the legality requirements in the original PRD, ADRs 0001 and 0003, and the authority, admission and consumer-visibility decisions. It removes any requirement for a legality authority or legality warnings in administrative review; complete inspection remains required for in-scope data and evidence. Existing issue discussions and completed implementation remain historical evidence, not requirements to preserve the removed capability.

The specification handoff must remove obsolete legality entities/projections, source-coverage dependencies, contracts, endpoints, CLI commands, export records, tests, smoke checks and freeze prerequisites together. Pre-Go-Live definitions change in place under ADR 0008. These planning/documentation changes do not claim that the current implementation has been removed or that existing runtime checks can already be skipped.

Publication applicability fencing for retained effective-dated corrections is still to be decided in this ticket; removal of legality does not itself settle that question.

## Owner-approved concurrency, captured facts and expiry policies

The owner agreed to concurrent collection across games and sources, with reconciliation, review and publication serialized per Supported Game. A refresh spanning games produces one independently reviewable Catalogue Candidate per game; atomic publication of a multi-game refresh is no longer required. Each candidate combines selected retained source evidence for its game. Same-game collection can continue while review is pending; newly collected evidence belongs in a later candidate rather than mutating the reviewed one.

Approval binds the exact candidate and expected Game Catalogue Revision. Publishing a different game does not invalidate that approval. A Catalogue Revision can identify a consistent composition of independently published Game Catalogue Revisions for reads and exports. This refines the global expected-revision wording in the earlier approval decision.

The owner explicitly rejected applicability-date invalidation: publish what the retained collected and reviewed data represents, without scheduled correction activation or continuous monitoring. Dates in retained corrections may remain evidence, but crossing them does not mutate or invalidate a candidate. Printed and publisher-corrected text remain separate; tournament eligibility remains outside scope. This replaces the former Reconciliation Clock applicability fence.

Transient interruptions use bounded automatic retries, then an inspectable pause preserving completed work. Explicit resume continues the operation; abandonment must fence late workers. Stale approval or corrupt evidence does not become valid through transport retries.

The seven-day deadline begins when the immutable candidate is created and is not extended by approval, retries or pauses. Expiry requires a fresh candidate and approval; reusable retained evidence/artifacts need not be discarded. Per-game predecessor changes remain a reason to reconcile and review again.

Cloudflare is preferred, external compute is permitted if investigation shows a material limitation, and cost-first durable background work is accepted. No numeric monthly spending ceiling or measured completion SLA has been set.

The architecture, capacity targets and backup interaction still need final review. This is an interim record of accepted policies, not the full resolution or closure of this decision ticket.

## Resolution — bounded, durable publication per game

Resolved through the owner's live answers, including the final architecture discussion and acceptance of the backup checkpoint and adjustable capacity targets. This is a planning decision; implementation and launch remain separate.

### Selected topology and alternatives

Start with Cloudflare Workers and Workflows for API entry points and bounded durable orchestration, R2 for immutable evidence/images/partitioned artifacts, and D1 for operation state, searchable projections and the final guarded publication transaction. Prefer cost-first background processing; external compute remains permissible if measured constraints justify it. No numeric monthly budget or completion SLA was agreed.

Queues and Durable Objects are not initial requirements. Queues could distribute independent image/partition work and buffer bursts; a Durable Object could coordinate per-hostname pacing or per-game work. Neither alone solves whole-catalogue buffering, nor replaces D1 publication guards. There is no measured benefit sufficient to require either now. Reassess against a concrete bottleneck or coordination simplification, accounting for duplicate delivery, dispatch/completion tracking and recovery. Concurrent collectors must share source-host pacing regardless of implementation; separate runs must not each consume the full source allowance.

### Concurrent collection and independent game publication

Allow collection across sources and games concurrently. Serialize reconciliation, review and publication per Supported Game. One game has one current candidate process, while new same-game collection may continue. Select and retain exact observations, admission/mapping decisions, source policy/profile versions and owner corrections at reconciliation; new evidence does not mutate that selection or silently supersede review.

Each candidate proposes one complete game revision, potentially assembled from several sources and collection runs. A refresh spanning games yields independently reviewable candidates. Multi-game atomic publication is explicitly replaced by per-game atomic publication. Approval binds the immutable candidate identity/digest and its expected Game Catalogue Revision, not the entire catalogue's prior composition. A same-game predecessor change requires fresh reconciliation and approval; another game's publication does not.

A Catalogue Revision identifies a consistent composition of Game Catalogue Revisions. Queries, pagination and exports pin that composition and consistently resolve its immutable data. Rejection, expiry or abandonment releases that game's candidate slot after fencing late writers. Supersession is explicit and never transfers approval to a replacement candidate.

### Immutable, partitioned preparation and complete inspection

Store image bytes and large artifacts independently with immutable references, lengths and integrity digests. Seal candidate content and a bounded hierarchical/partitioned manifest before review. Partition normalized records, relationships, mappings, administrative evidence, semantic differences, export components and search/query projection work. Do not replace an image-bearing whole-catalogue blob with a metadata-only whole-catalogue blob or one giant database batch.

Every reconciliation, comparison, image verification, export generation and projection stage must use bounded reads, writes and memory, durable progress and idempotent units. Large entities or high-degree relationships must be subdivided or rejected with an explicit capacity result, never silently truncated. Carry-forward should reuse immutable content where possible. Independently generated per-game exports are composed by references; publishing one game must not regenerate unrelated games' exports. Partition the composition index if necessary instead of embedding an unbounded game map in the commit.

Administration exposes the complete sealed candidate, before/after differences including evidence-only changes, inspectable images and retained evidence through consistently pinned pages. Summary counts must reconcile with detail pages; missing, corrupt or unfinished required artifacts block readiness. Approval is whole-candidate without mandatory per-item acknowledgement. Consumers receive accepted in-scope facts and explicit unknowns, without administrative evidence metadata.

### Durable operations, retries and deadlines

Reconciliation and approval/publication requests promptly return an operation identity and status location; the CLI's request deadline does not bound the background operation. Persist approval before acknowledging it. The same idempotency key and exact intent returns the same operation/result; incompatible reuse is rejected. Persist phase, progress, attempts, failure/pause reasons and published result outside short-lived Workflow history. A lost response is resolved through status or an idempotent retry, not a new publication.

Bounded automatic transient retries lead to an inspectable pause when exhausted. Explicit resume continues the same operation and reuses verified completed work. Corruption, stale predecessor, invalid evidence and expired approval are not transport failures to retry indefinitely. Durable ownership generations fence previous workers after recovery or abandonment; lease expiry alone never grants a stale worker authority. Owner abandonment prevents a late commit and does not delete audit evidence.

The original seven-day candidate deadline starts when the immutable candidate is created and continues through approval, backup waits, retries and pauses. It is rechecked at the final switch and is never extended by approval or resume. Expiry requires a fresh candidate and approval; retained evidence and safe immutable artifacts may be reused.

### Observed card content, without temporal activation or legality

The [owner-approved scope amendment](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/214#issuecomment-5558719187) removes tournament eligibility, ban lists, organised-play restrictions, FAQs and rulings while retaining Printed Rules Text and publisher-issued corrections alongside originals. It holds the complete scope replacement and affected-contract requirements.

The owner explicitly rejected the proposed applicability-date fence. Publish the retained collected/reviewed facts; do not implement scheduled correction activation, continuous monitoring or date-crossing invalidation. A stated date may remain source evidence, but crossing it does not recompute the candidate. Capture dates remain truthful per source; several captures are not presented as a single simultaneous observation. This replaces the old Reconciliation Clock applicability semantics, independently of the seven-day operational deadline.

### Final atomic visibility

Stage and verify all required objects/projections before the final switch. Perform a small database-enforced transaction checking immutable readiness, exact candidate/approval identity, current game predecessor, current composition, writer generation, deadline and recovery health. Atomically advance visible composition, record publication success and reserve the corresponding backup checkpoint. No catalogue-sized scan, artifact upload, projection generation or cleanup belongs in this transaction.

A failed compare-and-set must prevent all sibling mutations; a preflight SELECT followed by an unchecked batch is insufficient. Concurrent unrelated-game publication can require rebuilding only the bounded composition references and retrying the transaction, preserving the approved game's exact content, expected predecessor and deadline. Same-game changes cannot be automatically rebased. Readers see a complete earlier or later composition, never partial staged data. Replica/session handling must preserve pointer-to-data consistency.

### Backup and recovery checkpoint

Keep the existing substantive guarantee: after each publication, verify its backup by disposable restore before the next composition is published. Other games may continue collection, reconciliation, inspection, preparation and durable approval while that verification runs; their final switch waits for healthy recovery. Accepting an approval intent while verification runs revises the old blanket approval block without allowing publication to outrun recoverability. The original candidate deadline still applies while waiting.

Actual shared-database Catalogue Recovery remains a global mutation fence through verification and explicit owner acceptance. Backups bind a consistent composition/database snapshot and retained recovery evidence. Recovery must safely classify staged data and pending operations; it must not expose staging or promise preservation of work created after the restored snapshot. Retain existing identity/history and verified recovery protections. Do not introduce a new replay system or weaken recovery guarantees merely to remove this checkpoint.

### Cleanup and retention

Garbage collection is bounded, resumable and reference-aware. It may reclaim abandoned scratch/staging objects and incomplete multipart work only after writer fencing and proof that no live operation, retained candidate evidence, published/retained revision, export or recovery record needs them. Paused work is not automatically orphaned. Persist cleanup intent/results, and recheck eligibility before deletion so a retry or another game cannot lose shared content. Use a documented grace period in the implementation and respect multipart expiry. Candidate expiry does not authorize deleting audit evidence, source observations or recovery history. Existing guarded deletion/retention contracts remain unless the later specification explicitly replaces them.

### Adjustable engineering budgets and validation

The owner accepted these as initial targets and explicitly expects them to change with future requirements and measurement. They are not measured throughput, immutable schema limits or a permanent capacity promise. Record tuning and enforce revised budgets consistently; preserve boundedness, integrity and the approval/recovery guarantees.

| Unit | Initial target |
| --- | --- |
| Metadata partition | At most 1 MiB serialized and 500 records, whichever binds first |
| Working memory | At most 64 MiB peak isolate working set under representative concurrency |
| Durable work unit | Target at most 10 seconds CPU, 100 service calls, four concurrent object streams; configure explicit finite wall-time and retry budgets |
| D1 staging batch | At most 100 mutations and 1 MiB bound data, within per-statement parameter/row limits; target under one second p95, five-second operational ceiling |
| Final transaction | At most 20 statements and 64 KiB request payload, same latency target; no catalogue-sized work |
| Workflow shard | At most 1,000 planned steps and 5,000 planned service calls, accounting for retries and durable continuation |
| Export component | Independently addressable 8 MiB target; stream larger artifacts where required |
| D1 occupancy | Review storage topology before projected total exceeds 5 GB, including retained data, indexes and all permitted concurrent staging |
| Administration requests | Bounded metadata pages using the partition byte/record ceiling; operation starts/status target under two seconds p95 within the existing ten-second CLI deadline, excluding streamed artifact downloads |

Capacity validation must first pass the reproduced 128 × 100 KiB image case. Then exercise synthetic workloads of 10,000 Printings / 20,000 images / 5 GiB image bytes / 100 MiB structured data, and 100,000 Printings / 200,000 images / 50 GiB image bytes / 1 GiB structured data, with storage-guard results explicit. A guard-triggering test is not proof of successful capacity.

Alongside synthetic tests, retain and replay the complete declared English source coverage for an initially supported Bandai game with two sources, and actual Riftbound/second-publisher coverage. Establish measured record/image/byte counts and realistic amplification before claiming full-game capacity. The current dossier contains no full-game census or timing benchmark; configured request capacities are not observed catalogue counts.

Test full/no-change/incremental refreshes, carry-forward, very large entities/relationships, image-only and evidence-only changes, interruption at every durable boundary, duplicate/lost requests, exhausted retries/resume, supersession/abandonment with late workers, expiry after approval, same-game stale approval, unrelated-game composition contention, object corruption, partial staging, consistent paginated reads/exports, backup failure/retry, restore and reference-safe cleanup. A correction date passing without new observations must not trigger recomputation or invalidate approval. Record bytes, CPU, wall time, memory, rows/index/write amplification, service calls, billed dimensions and operator actions; establish completion/cost targets from those measurements.

### Evidence and handoff

The review baseline `60415d00da0ccbc843eb92d0c8f6545dd15271c4` reproduces a 17,526,322-byte candidate rejected by the real 16 MiB guard from 128 images × 100 KiB. Eager memory use, ten-second CLI timeout exposure, and whole-catalogue synchronous publication are code-path findings, not measured live throughput failures.

Current primary references: [Workflows limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/reference/limits/), [Workers limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/), [D1 limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/limits/), [D1 transactions](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/), [D1 read consistency](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/best-practices/read-replication/), [R2 consistency](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/reference/consistency/), [R2 uploads](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/objects/upload-objects/), [Queues delivery](https://developers.cloudflare.com/queues/reference/delivery-guarantees/), [Durable Objects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/concepts/what-are-durable-objects/). Cost analysis must include [Workflow steps/storage](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workflows/reference/pricing/), [D1](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/platform/pricing/) and [R2](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/pricing/), not CPU alone.

Local research asset: `docs/research/2026-09-06-bounded-publication-platform.md` in the working checkout, currently uncommitted. It holds the dated platform/pricing evidence and measurement gaps; it is not a measured capacity report. Domain docs are updated locally; the ADR pointer records this decision without duplicating its full policy.

[Decide validation, contract revisions, and specification handoff](https://github.com/KeeprDigital/card-keepr/issues/215) must carry these decisions into replacement contracts and acceptance tests, including per-game approval, captured-data semantics, adjustable budgets and the verified-backup checkpoint. It also owns the existing real-source evidence/validation follow-up; no new decision ticket is needed. The map's source-specific evidence fog remains. Only this decision ticket is resolved in this session; implementation, specification handoff and launch are not completed here.

title: Decide bounded durable reconciliation and publication
